item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"SCOPe’s current treatment means that 1br0 and 1ez3 should not be interpreted as independent, authoritative examples of their formerly fragment-derived fold assignments. Their partial structures are now understood in the context of the complete syntaxin N-terminal domain observed in 1dn1 chain B and should be classified with that domain. Thus, any topology or domain-boundary inference should use 1dn1B as the complete representative; the fragments can support local structural comparisons but not a distinct global fold, independent homology claim, or reliable full-domain template. Because the proteins are syntaxins, their association is appropriately interpreted at family-level evolutionary strength, whereas resemblance between an isolated fragment and proteins elsewhere in the same fold does not by itself justify family/superfamily homology or functional transfer. Functions should be transferred only with independent sequence and biological evidence, not from the fragment’s old fold placement alone.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
